headline: US Consumer Confidence Index Rises to 103.3 in November
summary: The Conference Board reported that its US consumer confidence index increased to 103.3 in November from 91.9 in October, buoyed by lower petrol prices.
why: US consumer spending accounts for over two-thirds of domestic economic output, making sentiment surveys key indicators of retail sales and growth trends.

impacts.name: United States
impacts.why: Higher consumer confidence signals resilient household spending and broader economic momentum.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Better-than-expected consumer confidence data reassured investors regarding economic growth resilience and retail spending prospects.
